summary: Manchester United drew 3-3 with Galatasaray in the Champions League after leading 2-0 and 3-1, the third time this season they have failed to win from a winning position. Erik ten Hag admitted the team isn't defending well enough, while captain Bruno Fernandes called for better game management. Pundits Gabby Agbonlahor and Rio Ferdinand blamed goalkeeper Andre Onana's errors and a lack of balance in the team.
one_line: Manchester United threw away another lead in a 3-3 Champions League draw with Galatasaray, prompting criticism of their defending, Onana and game management.
key_facts: Manchester United drew 3-3 with Galatasaray in the Champions League, damaging their bid to reach the last 16.
Alejandro Garnacho and Bruno Fernandes put United 2-0 up within 18 minutes before Hakim Ziyech pulled one back.
Scott McTominay scored shortly after the break to make it 3-1, but United failed to hold on.
Ziyech scored a second from a free-kick that Andre Onana let spill under him, and Kerem Akturkoglu equalised.
United must beat Bayern Munich and hope Galatasaray draw with FC Copenhagen on the final matchday to progress.
It is the third time this Champions League season United have been in a winning position and failed to win; they have dropped eight points from leads, more than any other team.
United have conceded 14 goals in the Champions League group stage, a new unwanted club record.
United's 12 group-stage goals are the fifth highest tally of any club.

Bruno Fernandes told TNT Sports that what United have done in the Champions League 'is not enough' and that they must control games and be smarter, citing the FC Copenhagen game where they led 3-2 against ten men.
Erik ten Hag said 'We aren't defending good enough, we are leading 3-1 and we can't afford such mistakes,' criticising himself and his coaching staff too.
Gabby Agbonlahor said that without Onana's two free-kick mistakes United would have won 4-1.
Rio Ferdinand said scoring nine goals in three away games for one point shows a lack of balance, and that United must erase the 'scars' from throwing away leads.
